history.body: Hi, saw the Pearl ad. My partner and I are renting now and just checking whether buying around here could make sense. What should we know?

Good place to start is what you’d want from owning that renting isn’t giving you. Pearl Residences’ Phase 1 homes are 900 sq.ft., with 3 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms and a balcony. For a couple, an extra room could be useful as a home office or for guests. Are you mainly considering buying to live in yourselves, or are you also weighing it as an investment?
For ourselves if we decide to buy. The monthly cost is what makes us unsure—one of us does freelance work, so income varies.

That’s a sensible concern, especially with freelance income varying. The confirmed maintenance rate is RM0.18 per sq.ft., inclusive of sinking fund—that’s one recurring cost, not the full ownership bill. I wouldn’t guess at a loan instalment without a current unit price and financing assumptions. A sensible first check is whether the full monthly commitment would still feel comfortable in a quieter income month. Is there a monthly ceiling you and your partner would want to stay under?
I haven’t worked out a ceiling yet; with the variable income, it depends on the price and financing. Is there a current starting price I could use as a reference?

As a rough price reference, the dated 14 August 2026 package snapshot works out to RM301,760 on a RM328,000 base for a qualifying Block 1B podium-blocked unit on Levels 1–4, after the listed 8% rebate. It isn’t a confirmed current offer or an all-in price: the exact unit, car-park configuration and any applicable add-ons need checking, along with the latest package. Would that price level be worth exploring for you both?
It’s a useful reference, but I can’t tell if it’s workable for us without current pricing and an idea of the monthly payment. With the variable income, we’d need to check carefully.

That’s sensible. The RM301,760 figure was only from a dated package snapshot, so I wouldn’t use it as today’s price. A monthly estimate also depends on the actual unit price and financing assumptions. I’ll get the latest pricing and a clearly qualified monthly-payment illustration checked, so you and your partner can assess affordability on a more realistic basis before deciding whether to proceed.
Okay, please share the latest pricing and payment illustration once confirmed. Then we can compare it with our rent and see whether it’s realistic for us.

Absolutely—I’ve requested the latest applicable pricing and a monthly-payment illustration with the assumptions clearly stated. The earlier figure was only a dated reference, so I’ll share the confirmed details once available for you both to compare with your rent.
